findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The arithmetic is supported by the quoted terms. Rent is GBP 1300 per calendar month, so annual rent is GBP 15,600. Five weeks of that is GBP 1,500.00, and the stated deposit is GBP 1,500, so the amount is at the cap and not above it. This is a correctly limited amount-cap pass. I found no counter-evidence that changes the amounts. Whether the cap applies at all is unresolved. The context lists jurisdiction and tenancy type as unknown, and the supplied text does not confirm the property is in England, that this is an ordinary private tenancy, or that the rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The Tenant Fees Act cap only covers qualifying tenancies. The cap result therefore stays conditional on those facts. Compliance with the amount cap says nothing about deposit protection or authenticity. s11 names a company client account as the payee, but that is a separate matter and this issue does not rely on it. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants
